title: Interconnect and communication latency in training
bottleneck: As training scales across tens of thousands of GPUs, communication — not computation — dominates: gradient synchronization and expert-parallel traffic saturate even the fastest interconnects, leaving expensive GPUs idle waiting for data. Scaling laws assume perfect parallelism, but real clusters achieve a fraction of theoretical FLOPS, and each doubling of cluster size buys less than double the effective compute.
why_it_blocks: The largest training runs are increasingly interconnect-limited, meaning money spent on GPUs is partly wasted on waiting — a tax on the entire scaling strategy.
current_state: New interconnect generations and parallelism strategies push the ceiling; hardware analyses flag interconnect latency as a first-order bottleneck alongside memory.
